goal: Implement the parry mechanic per docs/04-COMBAT_SYSTEM.md section 3.6. Pure function `evaluateParry(nowMs, attackCueMs, focus)` returns a `ParryResult` describing whether the defender parried the incoming cue, how much damage is mitigated, and whether a cue was stolen (criticals only). Surface shape matches the rhythm-window family so the battle scene can reuse its rendering hooks.
constraints: Pure function. No imports outside `./types` (RhythmQuality is allowed) and TypeScript built-ins.
Signature: `evaluateParry(nowMs: number, attackCueMs: number, focus: number): ParryResult`.

Define and export `ParryResult` as `{ quality: 'critical' | 'perfect' | 'good' | 'miss', incomingDamageMul: number, stoleCue: boolean, deltaMs: number }`. (Parry doesn't expose 'off' — it collapses to 'miss'.)

Windows (delta = |nowMs - attackCueMs|): critical ≤30ms, perfect ≤80ms, good ≤160ms, else miss. Note critical is TIGHTER than attack-side critical (40ms in 08); parry is harder by design per docs/04 §3.6.
Focus widening identical to rhythm-window: tolerance × (1 + min(focus,100)/200), max +50%.
Damage mitigation: critical=×0.0 (full negate), perfect=×0.3, good=×0.6, miss=×1.0.
`stoleCue` is true ONLY on critical parry — caller (battle-scene) uses this to add a bonus cue to its NEXT attack turn per docs/04 §3.6.
No mutation, no external state, JSDoc references docs/04 §3.6.
acceptance: Test covers every boundary (±1ms), every quality, focus=0 and focus=100.
Test verifies critical parry with focus=100 expands the window to ≤45ms.
Test verifies stoleCue is true on critical, false on every other quality.
